title: WPMS/314/2005 of RAMA KANT MEHROTRA and ORS. Vs ANAND SHANKER TRIPATHI and ANR.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition No. 314 (M/S) of 2005
 Rama Kant Mehrotra
 and three others - Petitioners
 Versus
 Anand Shankar Tripathi and another - Respondents
 Sri Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for the petitioners
 Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, Advocate holding brief of Mr. V.K. Kaprawan
 Advocate for respondent No.1.
 Sri K.C. Tewari, Brief Holder on behalf of respondent No.2.
[Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral)]
Heard Mr. Sudhir Kumar Advocate for the petitioners, Mr.
Bhuwan Bhatt, holding brief of Mr. V.K. Kaprawan, Advocate for
respondent No.1 and Mr. K.C. Tewari, Brief Holder on behalf of
respondent No.2.
 Counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of respondent No.1.
 Learned counsel appearing on behalf of parties have agreed that
this writ petition may be disposed of at the admission stage.
 By means of this petition the petitioners have sought the
following relief:-
(1) to pass an order setting aside the judgment dated 15-2-2005,
passed by respondent no.2, in Rent Control Case No. 3 of 2000,
Sushil Kumar Mehrotra and another versus Anand Shanker
Tripathi (contained in Annexure No. 9 to the writ petition).
(2) to direct the respondent No.1 to restore the amenity of latrine to
the petitioners by its reconstruction within such time as this
Hon'ble Court may grant and in the event of the respondent no.1
failing to comply with the directions of the Hon'ble Court the
petitioners be allowed to reconstruct the same at the costs and
expenses of the respondent No.1.
(3) award costs of the petition.
According to petitioners, respondent No.1 is landlord of the
premises known as Staff House Compound, Mallital, Nainital and the
petitioners are tenants in the premises in dispute on a monthly rent of

2
Rs. 287/-. Earlier Smt. Raj Rani wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of
petitioners 2 to 4 was the tenant of respondent No.1 in the premises in
dispute. She died on 2.5.2004 and the petitioners being her legal
representatives have inherited her tenancy rights in the premises in
dispute. Earlier the respondent No.1 filed a suit for her ejectment and
recovery of arrears of rent and damages for unauthorized use and
occupation. The suit was dismissed by the trial court and the matter is
pending before this High Court in revision. The respondent No.1 in
order to cause harassment and inconvenience and to force the
petitioners to vacate the premises in dispute, dismantled the latrine.
An application for restoration of this amenity was moved before the
Prescribed Authority Nainital, respondent No.2, which was registered
as Rent Case No.3 of 2000. The said application was moved on behalf
of Smt. Raj Rani, the tenant and her son, the petitioner No.4, who was
living in the premises in dispute at the relevant time. But due to some
mistake the application was not signed and verified by Smt. Raj Rani.
An application for correction of this mistake was made to respondent
No.2. The said application was allowed by respondent No.2 by order
dated 29-4-2004. In the mean time Smt. Raj Rani died on 2.5.2004
and application for substitution of the names of petitioners was made.
The application for substitution was allowed by the respondent No.2
vide order dated 12-8-2004. Smt. Raj Rani had also filed an affidavit
in the case during her life time and the petitioner No.4 also filed his
affidavit in support of the application for restoration of amenity.
However, the respondent No.2 has rejected the application of the
petitioners for restoration of amenity by his order dated 15.2.2005.
The learned Prescribed Authority in his order has observed that
in the application filed under Section 27 of U.P. Act No.13 of 1972
for restoration of amenity signatures of Smt. Raj Rani have not been
made. It is the case of petitioners that during pendency of the
application Smt. Raj Rani has died and her legal heirs have already
been substituted by the order of respondent No.2.
 Therefore, in the above facts and circumstances of the case, the
writ petition is allowed. The impugned judgment dated 15.2.2005 is
set aside and the matter is remanded back to respondent
No.2/Prescribed Authority/C.J.M. Nainital, to decide the case on its

3
merits after giving opportunity of hearing to both the parties, in
accordance with law, expeditiously, as far as possible.
ISB (B.S. Verma, J.)
 26-03-2012
